body:
COLLAB ACCEPTED TWO, DECLINED THE THIRD, AND THE SUCCESSORS ARE IN. Their words: yes to d917218 and
067e35b, "please ask another live reviewer for 0ca09c5" because its align/codec/laws/goldens surface
needs capacity they cannot promise while the movie ledger artifact is moving. Review only, not
authorization, not path ownership - their framing, and correct.

  cand-6VN2GFNJZSDW5Y1PDRAB6X61PY  067e35b  reviewer collab   supersedes cand-15R9779T...
  cand-4CSV7DTJY759BKMBYCFSGA7G0J  d917218  reviewer collab   supersedes cand-71JAQ9YZ...
Both old rows now read `superseded`. Both new rows refreshed; each has exactly two blockers,
authorization_absent and review_missing, counted with grep -c before I looked at them.

I MUST CORRECT SOMETHING I TOLD YOU EARLIER ABOUT supersede. I reported that it failed on scout's row
because of PROPOSER OWNERSHIP. That was a guess dressed as a diagnosis. The error names three
conditions at once:

    supersede requires proposer ownership, current phase CAS, and a distinct pending
    same-repository successor

and it failed identically on MY OWN rows, which I do own. THE ACTUAL CAUSE WAS THE CAS ARGUMENT:
`--expect-phase` wants the phase's OP_ID, not the literal string "pending". With the op_id
(`20260830T022319.603159Z-p83228-...`) both superseded immediately. I picked the plausible clause
out of a three-clause message and reported it as the finding, which is the same error as reading a
truncated blocker list an hour ago - a compound condition, one branch assumed.

SO THE STATUS OF SCOUT'S ROW IS NOW UNKNOWN TO ME, not "blocked on ownership". Ownership may still be
the real blocker there, or it may have been the same CAS mistake. I AM NOT GOING TO FIND OUT BY
TRYING, because the only experiment is mutating another actor's row, and a successful supersede of
scout's candidate by me is not an outcome I should be able to produce accidentally. If you want it
tested, test it or authorise someone to.

For your AGENTS.md pass, if it is worth a line alongside the `[ ]` redirect one: `mote candidate
supersede --expect-phase` takes the phase op_id as a CAS token. Your unblocking script said "then
supersede cand-0PDQ..." with no token, so anyone following it literally hits a three-clause error
and will most likely blame the clause that sounds most like their situation - which is what I did.

REMAINING: 0ca09c5 still needs a reviewer. Live and eligible are new-engineer and
movie-architecture; movie-architecture is deep in the film ledger, so I will ask new-engineer next
unless you would rather assign it. All three still need your authorization.
